issues.legal_issue: An acquiring public authority cannot obtain a complete stay of enhanced compensation merely because it lacks funds or acquired land for a public purpose, and must pay the compensation determined on reference or restore the land if it cannot pay.
material_facts: The authority acquired agricultural land, took possession after paying the compensation initially awarded, and the reference court later enhanced the compensation.
The authority appealed the reference court’s award and obtained a conditional stay of execution requiring it to pay 50% of the enhanced compensation, but it did not make that payment.
The authority sought a stay of all payment, relying on the public purpose of the acquisition and its inability to pay; enforcement proceedings continued.
The Supreme Court directed the authority to pay the enhanced compensation or, failing that, restore possession to the affected landowners, who would refund the compensation they had received.
issues.conclusion: The authority’s appeals were dismissed. Its lack of funds and the public purpose of the acquisition did not justify withholding the enhanced compensation; it was required to pay the enhanced amount or restore possession, with the landowners refunding the compensation already received.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the Collector’s award is an offer on behalf of the State, while the reference court determines market value after considering the evidence. Possible variation in valuation does not justify staying the operation of the reference court’s award in full. Article 300A protects the right to property, and the authority’s public purpose or financial difficulty does not justify depriving affected persons of compensation. Payment of the initial award is not sufficient security pending an appeal against the reference court’s award; if the acquiring party cannot pay compensation, the aggrieved person becomes entitled to restoration of the land. The Court relied on Girish Vyas v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2012 SC 2043; Raju S. Jethmalani v. State of Maharashtra, (2005) 11 SCC 222; Tukaram Kana Joshi v. Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation, AIR 2013 SC 565; K. Krishna Reddy v. Special Deputy Collector, AIR 1988 SC 2123; Narain Das Jain v. Agra Nagar Mahapalika, (1991) 4 SCC 212; Mahanadi Coal Fields Ltd. v. Mathias Oram, (2010) 11 SCC 269; and Narmada Bachao Andolan v. State of Madhya Pradesh, AIR 2011 SC 1989.

rule.if: appeal_against_reference_award and acquiring_authority_retains_possession and reference_court_enhanced_compensation and authority_failed_conditional_payment and authority_claims_inability_to_pay

predicates.appeal_against_reference_award: The acquiring authority appealed against a reference court’s determination of enhanced compensation.
predicates.acquiring_authority_retains_possession: The acquiring authority took possession of the land and continued to retain it.
predicates.reference_court_enhanced_compensation: The reference court awarded compensation greater than the initial award.
predicates.authority_failed_conditional_payment: The acquiring authority did not make the payment required as a condition of the stay of execution.
predicates.authority_claims_inability_to_pay: The acquiring authority said it could not pay the enhanced compensation because it lacked funds.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority retains land after a reference court enhances compensation, fails to make a required conditional payment, and claims it cannot pay while appealing the award, it must pay the compensation or restore the land on refund.

issues.legal_issue: A delayed appeal may be admitted after the court condones the delay.
material_facts: The authority filed its appeals 308 days late.
The authority’s counsel could not explain the circumstances justifying the delay.
The Supreme Court condoned the delay and granted leave to appeal.
issues.conclusion: The delay was condoned and leave to appeal was granted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court condoned the delay but stated no legal test or earlier case governing that decision.

predicates.appeal_filed_after_delay: The appellant filed its appeal after the applicable filing period had passed.

issues.definition: If an appeal is filed after a delay, the output in this case was that the delay was condoned.
